title: The Refutation of All Heresies
author: hippolytus
attributionNote: The attribution is recorded as the edition and the scholarly consensus give it; where the attribution is disputed, the work says so.
description: A survey of philosophical schools and Christian heresies, arguing that the Gnostic systems derived from Greek philosophy. It preserves extensive quotations from Valentinian, Naassene, Sethian and other teaching, and is a central source for Gnostic thought despite its hostile frame.
historicalContext: Transmitted under the name of Hippolytus of Rome; the attribution is debated. Books II and III are lost. The text reflects the theological conflicts of early third-century Rome.
availabilityNote: Streamed from the Christian Classics Ethereal Library at read time. MacMahon's translation from the Ante-Nicene Fathers, served by the CCEL. The attribution to Hippolytus is disputed and is recorded as such, not settled here.
